title: help
author: No_Statistician9051
selftext: i am completely new to trading and i basically know almost nothing. ive been seeing videos online about ai trading and ai trading bots that tell u where to sell and buy etc. im just wondering does it actually work or is it a scam and has anyone here tried it and profited from it. im fine with paying a little for the ai trading bots but i really want to know if it actually works or is it fake and whether u can really make a lot of money with it. and if it actually works how can i get started and how long does it usually take to actually see an increase in profit

comments.author: p3r3lin
comments.body:
Without deep knowledge and access to gated data you will probably not be able to beat a buy and hold strategy. Dont fall for people trying to sell you anything that sounds to good to be true. AI can be a great help for traders, but you would need to know what you are doing and how to utilize an AI. 

Maybe start with using AI to learn about trading. Its very good at explaining things!

comments.author: Affectionate-Fun-623
comments.body: My advice is If you’re starting, Learn first. Don’t start trading right now. Develop a strategy you can call your own or get strategy ideas from others. There’s lots of strategy guids on youtube some of them work but optimization and execution matters which is entirely up to you. So develop your strat, paper trade- paper trade- paper trade until you are confident with your execution. Then paper trade some more. I can’t urge this enough. Don't enter with real money until you are consistently green on paper trading. Pick your assets, dont trade all over. Two more topics to learn about which are very very important.  Risk management (risk-reward ratio) and revenge trading. These topics have lots of videos on youtube. Last but not least, If you can't control your emotions, don’t enter this field. You will lose money at first cause you’re a noob (we were all noobs once). So no crying in the casino.

replies.author: Affectionate-Fun-623
replies.body: Don’t look at complicated youtube tutorials selling courses or big playlists that teach you lots of stuff without really teaching anything. You’re not trying to get job at a trading firm so remember “simple is better”

replies.author: Affectionate-Fun-623
replies.body: Look for a simple strategy. Just one, you can look at the 9am market shift strategy if you’re still not sure which to trust. Works good on Forex assets and it’s backed up by real research papers. After choosing a strategy try to use it and see how you do.

replies.author: Affectionate-Fun-623
replies.body: Also, AI trading is not a scam. You can use AI as a tool to creat bots and analyse the market for you. Depends on the models and how you train it if you’re going for local AIs. But actually giving AI the autonomy to make decisions and make trades for you is a different ballpark. But any one of these topics takes months of research and testing testing testing. So don’t expect to get rich overnight. The market is a tough place and there is nothing called easy money. People who say easy money are trying to sell you something which didn’t make them money. Remember that someone who is actually making shit load of money in the market won’t tell you how he is making it.

replies.author: speedalyst
replies.body: Can you provide a link to more details on 9am market shift strategy. Mahalo from Hawaii.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Most of those bots are selling you a signal, not an edge. If the thing actually printed money, they wouldn't need your subscription. The videos are marketing, the backtests are usually curve-fit, and the live results never match. You can learn trading without paying for a bot first. Paper trade for a few months, track every call honestly, and see if you even beat just holding an index. That answer will tell you more than any bot demo.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: most of those videos are selling the bot, not running it, and nobody can tell you how long before one pays off because plenty never do. before paying anyone, run the idea on fake money for a month and watch what it actually does. I built a free tool for that, Quantradin, it covers American stocks plus their options with pretend money. quantradin.com

comments.author: TheAgentFloor
comments.body: The tools that promise to tell you exactly when to buy and sell are the ones I would be most careful with, especially anything sold with screenshots of big gains. From what I can tell, the AI itself is not the edge. It follows whatever strategy it is given, and if the strategy is bad it just loses money faster and without emotion. If you want to try it, I think the lowest risk way to start is paper trading with fake money for a while, so you can see how it behaves before real money is involved. Alpaca and a few others have free paper accounts for this.

comments.author: SalvaFa93
comments.body:
Before paying anyone, run four questions on the bot. If the seller cannot answer one of them with evidence, walk away:



1. Do they show every trade, losses included, not a selection of screenshots?

2. Was each call published with a time on it before the move, or explained afterwards?

3. Is there a period after the model was frozen, with no tweaks, where you can see how it did on data it had never seen?

4. Can you check the results yourself on a public price chart, bar by bar?



And one rule that saves the most money: anyone who tells you how long it takes to "see profit", or how much you will make, is selling the promise, not the tool. Nobody honest can answer that question, with AI or without.



Disclosure, so you can weigh this: I am building an AI market-analysis product, not a bot, and those four questions are the standard we hold ourselves to. If a tool passes all four, it is worth a closer look. Most of what is sold to beginners fails the first one.
